title: Manufacturer-imposed requirements (Guide to Antitrust Laws: Dealings in the Supply Chain)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Vertical price programmes judged under the rule of reason since a 2007 Supreme Court decision; a manufacturer acting alone may deal only with retailers that follow its policy ('take it or leave it'); suggested prices fine if the dealer decides independently; some state laws and international authorities treat minimum price rules as per se illegal; FTC challenge to MAP policies of five music distributors; co-op advertising latitude.

title: Leegin Creative Leather Products, Inc. v. PSKS, Inc. (syllabus)
publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Decided 28 June 2007; overruled Dr. Miles; vertical price restraints judged under the rule of reason; possible procompetitive effects (retailer services, interbrand competition) and anticompetitive effects (facilitating cartels).

title: Price discrimination: Robinson-Patman violations
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Covers commodities not services; defences of cost justification and meeting competition; promotional allowances and services must be offered to competing customers on proportionally equal terms, and all must be informed.

title: Antitrust laws and you
publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 20 Dec 2023). Agreements among competitors to fix prices, rig bids or allocate customers or markets are criminal violations of the Sherman Act.

title: Resale price maintenance: advice for retailers
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last updated 29 Jun 2020). Definition of RPM; RRPs lawful while retailers are free to set prices; restricting discounts, minimum advertised price policies and linking prices to competitors are indirect RPM; supplier and retailer can both break the law; fear of losing a supplier is no defence; Dar Lighting GBP 1.5 million and GAK GBP 278,945 (agreement with Yamaha) fines.

title: Restricting resale prices: an open letter to suppliers and retailers in the musical instruments sector
supports: Opened with WebFetch (published 29 Jun 2020). The CMA imposed fines totalling more than GBP 13.7 million across five cases in the sector for restricting online discounting.

title: GBP 4.5 million fine for Fender for illegally preventing online price discounts
supports: Opened with WebFetch (case study dated 29 Jun 2020). Minimum resale prices January 2013 to April 2018; threats of delayed orders, less credit and withdrawn marketing support; highest UK RPM fine at the time; fines up to 10% of global turnover; resellers can also be investigated and fined.

title: Business cartels case studies
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Lists CMA case studies including Dar Lighting GBP 1.5 million (2022), Roland GBP 4 million, Korg GBP 1.5 million, Fender GBP 4.5 million and Casio GBP 3.7 million (2020), all for preventing online price discounts.

title: Competition rules in the EU
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last checked 12 Jul 2026). Lists distribution agreements between suppliers and resellers where the price charged to customers is imposed by the supplier among prohibited practices.

title: Vertical block exemptions
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/720 of 10 May 2022 entered into force on 1 June 2022; the 2010 regulation expired on 31 May 2022; Vertical Guidelines published in OJ C 248, 30 Jun 2022.

title: Solutions Partner Program
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 20% commission for 3 years on deals partners bring; 20% for 1 year on certain co-sold deals started by HubSpot sales; programme package fee and waiver; directory listing and certifications.

title: Xero partner program for accountants and bookkeepers (US)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Free programme; levels Partner, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum; benefits by level (practice management from Silver, subscription discounts from Bronze); at least one staff member to complete Xero advisor certification within 30 days; advisor directory listing.

title: Register your deals (Partner Center)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 21 Jul 2026). Co-sell eligibility USD 25,000 or more; ISV Connect over USD 5,000; register within 60 days of contract signature; wait 72 hours before marking won; manual review over USD 1 million, multiple partners or pay-as-you-go; one exception request per referral, up to 14 working days, final.

title: AWS Partner funding programs
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Marketing Development Funds offset demand generation and pipeline costs as cash or AWS Promotional Credits; MDF requests need an AWS Payee Central account with bank registration and tax interview complete.

title: B2B (Shopify Help Center)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. B2B on Basic, Grow, Advanced and Shopify Plus, not Starter or Retail; companies with their own pricing, currency, products, payment and shipping; B2B and D2C in one store or a separate B2B store.

title: Catalogs in B2B (Shopify Help Center)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Catalogs include or exclude products, apply percentage adjustments and fixed prices; volume pricing and quantity rules; up to 3 active catalog assignments on Basic, Grow and Advanced; direct assignment to company locations on Plus.

title: B2B payment terms (Shopify Help Center)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Net 7, 15, 30, 45, 60 or 90; due on fulfilment; fixed date; deposits on Plus; payments not captured automatically when terms expire; orders show as overdue.

title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: what people are asking
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Affiliates earning commission must disclose clearly and close to the recommendation; 'affiliate link' alone may not be clear; the company is ultimately responsible for what others do on its behalf and should train and monitor.

title: Affiliate marketing (advice online)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (advice dated 22 Mar 2023). Affiliate content falls under the CAP Code; must be obviously identifiable upfront ('Ad'); 'affiliate' not widely understood; brand and affiliate both responsible; rulings listed with dates.

title: Business guidance concerning multi-level marketing
supports: Opened with WebFetch (dated April 2024). Pyramid where rewards come from recruiting unrelated to sales to real customers; retail customers not a safe harbour; inventory loading; earnings claims need reliable evidence.

title: Late commercial payments: charging interest and debt recovery
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Agreed payment usually within 60 days for business transactions (longer if fair), 30 days for public authorities; with no agreed date, late 30 days after invoice or delivery, whichever is later.

title: Late payment
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last checked 5 Aug 2026). Interest automatically payable 30 days after the invoice where no period is set; flat EUR 40 compensation per late invoice; statutory rates by country for 1 Jul to 31 Dec 2026 (for example Germany 10.52%).

title: HubSpot MCP Server
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Remote MCP server at mcp.hubspot.com; lists read and write access to CRM objects including contacts, companies and deals, but also mentions read-only access to standard records; OAuth with scoped user-level apps.
